text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State-owned Nigerian Telecommunications Limited last year awarded 20 billion naira contracts for digital telephone lines, says its managing director in company's newsletter NITEL News.
- First Lady Maryam Abacha launches Family Economic Advancement Programme to give loans worth 4.3 billion naira this year to small entrepreneurs to boost cottage industries.

- Staff of the Department of Petroleum Resources which oversees Nigeria's oil export start new campaign to get the authorities to dump external inspectors engaged last year to check alleged fraud in loading Nigerian crude oil.
- Army fortifies defence headquarters in Lagos by installing anti-terrorist equipment there following wave of bomb blasts in the country.
- The former interim head of state and chairman of Vision 2010 group planning Nigeria's future, Ernest Shonekan, says sanctions imposed by the West on Nigeria "are somewhat hurting".
- Forty-eight newly listed stock broking firms are to each pay a mandatory one million naira to an investors protection fund within 30 days or lose their licences.
- Children constitute 45 percent of Nigeria's population of 100 million, says planning minister Ayo Ogunlade.
- State oil firm NNPC suspends three unnamed officials over alleged fraud involving overloading of vessels with oil products and pocketing the proceeds.

- Nigerian government may have decided to license three privately owned global systems of mobile communications and eight national and regional telephone networks to compete with state-owned Nigerian Telecommunications Ltd, sources say.
- Nigerian government may soon re-award some of the crude oil lifting contracts terminated early in 1996, oil sources say.

- Foreign investors are still interested in doing business in Nigeria despite news of political instability in the country, says newly elected president of Nigeria-European Association Harry Kroop, a Dutch businesman.
- Central bank sold treasury bills worth a total of 234.8 billion naira in 1996, says its director of research M.O. Ojo.
